new_results.statement: For n=4m>=8, the balanced flat frame r0,rv,ru has leverage 3/n; arbitrary diagonal twist plus nonzero three-mode coefficients a,b,c has continuous output density bounded by 12|abc|^-1/3. This covers both (+,+,-) and (+,-,-) coefficient signatures without post-rotation independence.

For the latest partner family A_delta=(1-2delta)J+delta vv^T-delta uu^T+2delta I in its target-valid range delta(n-2)>=1, ||p||inf<=9/4^(1/3)=5.6696447245..., although every fixed physical packet can degenerate.
For n=8m>=16, an equal sign-class split with actual cross block R_I diag(a,b,c) R_J^T gives ||p_Q||inf<=12sqrt(e)|abc|^-1/3, with arbitrary same-side blocks, outside couplings and affine terms.

For the same balanced cut, if the actual cross block differs from R_I diag(a,b,c)R_J^T by operator norm at most mu/32, mu=min(|a|,|b|,|c|), then ||p_Q||inf<46/mu; this is a matrix-level Fourier stability statement, not a small-random-variable perturbation.

rank_two_control: In the same four-bank Walsh geometry, V^2-U^2=(4/n)(S_{++}-S_{--})(S_{-+}-S_{+-}); the two factors use disjoint original-coordinate banks. For centered unit uniforms their product density diverges logarithmically at zero. Algebraic Schur removal of the third common mode leaves exactly this opposite-sign saddle. The third mode removes the divergence analytically by changing joint Fresnel decay from the nonintegrable |t|^-1 endpoint to |t|^-3/2 in the original-coordinate product integral.
unresolved_implication: QFORM-BALANCED-CROSSCUT-STABILITY-v1: in a general unfrustrated near-rank-one N3 survivor with no fixed packet, force a growing original-coordinate cut with target-scale third volume and admissible marginals (possibly after operator stability), or a low-leverage three-mode plus diagonal product bank, or an already-paid scalar/pair/sign-frustration/ridge/hub exit. The account03/B11 r26 family is the normalization test.
